summary: Iteration 2 backend testing for PestOps Pro. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py with 31 tests covering: 4-role logins (admin/tech/client/developer), tech/client permission maps, schedules mass-create (weekday filter), schedules CRUD, Nominatim geocode search/reverse, customer creation with linked client user (+ login), task filters (customer_id/date range), client-scoped tasks + client GPS-ping 403, attendance check-in with reverse-geocoded address + check-out with working_hours (verified check-in doc is updated with checkout_id/working_hours), service-report photos (documented duplicate-field bug), SR client_signature, SR listing filters, client-scoped SRs, bulk ZIP export (PK header + application/zip), monthly-report data (historical spans contract_start→target, SRs only from target month) + PDF, branding GET/PUT (dev allowed, tech 403), email endpoints (400 when no recipient; 200/502/500 accepted for provider). 30/31 pass. The 1 failure is an intentional assertion that exposes a real backend bug (see rca).

critical.issue: ServiceReportCreate model (server.py:171-181) declares `photos` TWICE — first as `List[SRPhoto]` (with captions), immediately overridden by `photos: List[str] = []`. Because Python class body assignments are last-write-wins, Pydantic v2 sees only `List[str]`. Sending [{path, caption}, ...] returns 422 (`string_type`), so the entire multi-photo-with-captions feature described in the requirements is non-functional. Reproduced with test test_photos_with_captions_bug. Fix: remove the duplicate legacy line 181.

minor.issue: When role=client, backend sets query['customer_id'] = client.customer_id, but a subsequent `if customer_id:` overwrites it if the client passes a customer_id query param. In practice the client will still see nothing (query no longer matches their scope), but the scoping is bypassed. If the client passes their OWN customer_id it works; if they pass another customer_id, they see rows of that customer (only if any tasks/SRs exist there for them). Recommend: apply query param filter first, then hard-override with client's customer_id, or 403 if mismatched customer_id.

Uses CustomerCreate as body model — client_email/client_password can be passed to update but the code only creates a linked client user on POST. Also PUT overwrites ALL customer fields (no PATCH), and does not popped client_email/client_password before update, so those get stored on the customer doc.

Uses `reverse_geocode()` which calls external Nominatim inside the request path — high latency + rate-limit exposure per check-in. Nominatim TOS also requires ≤1 req/s. Should be cached or moved to a background task.

No conflict/duplicate detection — running twice with same params silently creates 2× schedules. Also allows creating schedules on already-past dates. Consider dedupe by (customer_id, technician_id, date, start_time).

Signature `body: SendReportEmail = Body(...)` alongside two other `Body(...)` params — works only because clients pass a nested `body` object; this is inconsistent with /service-reports/{id}/email which uses SendReportEmail as top-level body. Confusing dual shape. Standardize.
No permission gate at all — any authenticated user can read branding. That's likely fine but should be explicit.
Body is raw dict (no Pydantic model); any key from the request is persisted into settings doc, including malicious keys or the `updated_at` client can set. Add a strict BrandingUpdate model.
CORS still `allow_origins=['*']` + `allow_credentials=False` — httpOnly `access_token` cookie set at login cannot be used cross-origin (same finding as iteration 1).
server.py grew to 1793 lines — should be split into routers (schedules, geocode, monthly_report, bulk_export, email, branding).

action_items: CRITICAL: Remove the duplicate `photos: List[str] = []` line in ServiceReportCreate (server.py line 181). Keep only `photos: List[SRPhoto] = []` so captions are actually accepted. Also update the SR list-enrichment / PDF paths to handle the {path,caption} shape (bulk zip PDF + monthly PDF already handle dict shape, so they'll start receiving real data once schema is fixed).

Fix client-scope bypass: in list_tasks / list_sr / list_schedules, apply the query-param customer_id BEFORE the role-based override, or reject with 403 when client passes a customer_id that isn't theirs.
Add a strict BrandingUpdate Pydantic model for PUT /api/branding.
Standardize /api/monthly-report/email request shape (either full flat SendReportEmail or nested — pick one and document).
Consider adding rate-limiting / caching to geocode endpoints and to reverse_geocode() called on every checkin.
Split server.py into feature routers (approaching 1800 lines).
critical_code_review_comments: Duplicate Pydantic field `photos` in ServiceReportCreate silently disables the multi-photo-with-captions feature (root cause of the 1 failing test).
Client role scope override is not hard-enforced — passing `?customer_id=OTHER` is not blocked with a 403, only silently overwritten (partial isolation).
PUT /api/tasks and PUT /api/branding accept arbitrary raw dicts — no field validation. Any unknown key gets stored.
reverse_geocode() called synchronously (awaited) in every attendance check-in / check-out — introduces external-service latency and rate-limit dependency into hot path.
Nominatim proxy has no caching and passes user-supplied `q` directly — high risk of 429s in production.
server.py = 1793 lines; the iteration 1 comment about splitting into routers is now more urgent.
CORS remains allow_origins=['*'] + allow_credentials=False while login still writes httpOnly cookie — cookie flow unusable cross-origin (same as iter1).

Two pytest files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (iter1 regression, 23 tests) and /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py (iter2, 31 tests). Run both. JUnit at /app/test_reports/pytest/. The single failing test in iter2 (TestServiceReportPhotos::test_photos_with_captions_bug) will start passing automatically once the duplicate `photos` field in ServiceReportCreate is removed (server.py:181). No email actually sent because provider returned 502 (EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY may be inactive) — test accepts 200/502/500 and passes on auth+ownership+400 path.
rca of the issue: ServiceReportCreate (server.py lines 171-181) declares the field `photos` twice: first as `List[SRPhoto] = []` (the intended multi-photo+caption schema), then immediately as `photos: List[str] = []` labelled `legacy - kept for backward compat`. In Python/Pydantic, the second class attribute assignment wins, so the model's schema only recognizes list-of-strings. Any request sending [{'path': ..., 'caption': ...}, ...] is rejected with 422 `string_type`. This makes the entire multi-photo-with-captions requirement non-functional at the API layer. Reproduction: POST /api/service-reports with photos=[{path,caption}] as tech token → 422. Mitigation: delete line 181 of server.py so only the SRPhoto schema remains. The downstream `_generate_monthly_pdf` already expects the dict shape (checks `isinstance(p, dict) and p.get('path')`), so removing the duplicate should Just Work end-to-end.
